sections.content: Any registered Georgia voter can apply for an absentee ballot (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/VoterInformation.htm?_ga=2.146035388.923513671.1717430095-1475019010.1654737627). You can apply for your absentee ballot online, by mail, email, fax or deliver it in person to your county registrar. Your voted ballot must be received by your county board of registrars by 7pm on Election Day to be counted.
Ballot curing is when a voter corrects an issue with their ballot, so it can be counted.

Click here to visit the Georgia Government Transparency and Campaign Finance Commission (https://media.ethics.ga.gov/Search/Campaign/Campaign_ByName.aspx) website. For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).
Candidate and ballot information can be found here. (https://www.vote411.org/vote411.org/ballot)

Early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins on October 13th and ends October 30th.

Early Voting Starts: The fourth Monday prior to Election Day. Contact your county elections office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more details.

Early Voting Ends: The Friday before Election Day. Contact your county elections office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more details.

Your next election date can be found here https://www.vote411.org/georgia.

For more election information contact your county clerk. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)
Polls are open from 7:00 am until 7:00 pm on Election Day. Any voter who is waiting in line to vote at 7:00 pm will be allowed to vote.

You are a Military or Overseas voter if you are in uniformed services, living overseas OR a spouse or dependent of a uniformed services voter. To get registered and vote, you can utilize Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

If you have additional questions about elections and voting overseas you can use our state specific elections official directory or contact the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource (https://www.mvp.sos.ga.gov/MVP/mvp.do). If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your county clerk. (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

Georgia is an “open primary” state. You can choose the party’s ballot you wish to vote. This decision does not register you with that party and it is a private decision.

In a primary election if a candidate does not with the majority of the votes (50%+1) there will be a primary runoff election scheduled for a few weeks after the primary election date. The runoff election will have the top two vote getters to ensure that one of them receives the majority of the voters.

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

To verify your voter registration status

  click here!  (http://www.mvp.sos.ga.gov/)
